chunks: He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Nahwi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Abu Hatim narrated to us, from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said:

Nabighah al-Ja'di was among those who worshipped God during the pre-Islamic era. He rejected wine and intoxication, and abandoned idols and divining arrows. He said during the pre-Islamic era his famous statement: "All praise belongs to God, Who has no partner; whoever does not say so has wronged himself." He used to profess the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and the Hanifiyyah, and he would fast and seek forgiveness. He would avoid things in which people indulged. He went as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, and said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah when he brought the guidance, and he recites a Book spread like the Milky Way. And I strove until I and my companions could no longer perceive the Canopus star when it appeared and then disappeared. And I turned to piety and did not fear any disbeliever, and I was from the frightful Fire more restrained."

He said: Nabighah was Alawite in his views, and after the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, he went with the Commander of the Believers, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, to Siffin. He alighted one night and was straitened by the situation, and he said: "The two Misrs and Iraq well know that 'Ali is their highborn stallion. Bright and a great leader with a pavilion, and his mother's dowry was high. The most honourable among those for whom a belt was tightened. Indeed those who competed with you have not come to their senses. You have your field of competition and they have theirs, and your companions well know this. You have driven to the path of guidance, while they have driven to that which has no foundation, in a creed whose habit is hypocrisy."

key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّة: The pre-Islamic era of ignorance, before the coming of Islam
key_terms.الْحَنِيفِيَّة: Hanifiyyah — the pure monotheistic religion of Prophet Ibrahim
key_terms.صِفِّين: Siffin — the major battle between Ali and Mu'awiyah in 37 AH
key_terms.عَلَوِيّ الرَّأْي: Alawite in opinion — supporter of Ali ibn Abi Talib's claim to leadership

ai.seo_question: Who was Nabighah al-Ja'di and how did he support Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration provides a biographical account of Nabighah al-Ja'di, a pre-Islamic monotheist poet who rejected idol worship and alcohol before Islam. He embraced Islam, met the Prophet, and later supported Imam Ali at the Battle of Siffin. His poetry praising Ali's nobility and denouncing Ali's opponents reflects the partisan literary tradition within early Islamic history.
